WHERE IT LANDS, CONFIRMED BEFORE BRIEFING. The named file is the intro block of templates/page.brightening-glow.json, section `content` (media-with-text), block `intro`, titled 'Understanding Skin Brightness & Glow' — recorded in configs/banners/page-brightening-glow-intro-image.json, which put it there earlier today. It is the only place that file is used. The image it currently holds is the cpr-sat slot-D portrait: a woman in her forties, fingertips at her cheekbone, looking up and away. This wave answers the three things Malcolm changed about it — YOUNGER (30-35, not forties), SMILING (it is barely a smile now), and GLOWING (the present frame is handsome but matte).

MASTER IS SQUARE, 2048x2048, and that is not a style choice. In media-with-text the row height is max(text column, image natural height) and .media-with-text__media carries no aspect-ratio of its own, so any non-square master stretches this row taller than its five siblings. The block was measured as a set when the current picture went in: it renders 1.000 at 1440 and 0.974 at 1024, so the cover-crop is negligible and no object-position rule is needed.

SIX SLOTS, BECAUSE VARIETY CANNOT COME FROM THE SUPPLIERS. generate-multi.py sends ONE prompt per slot to every backend, so all six candidates of a slot necessarily share the woman, the light and the crop that prompt names — the structural fault that cost the acetyl selfie wave four rounds. Real alternatives therefore have to be six separate briefs. Each slot is a different woman, a different lighting setup and a different crop; six suppliers, one candidate each, is thirty-six pictures.

SKIN TONE RANGE IS DELIBERATE AND THE PAGE ASKS FOR IT. This page's own FAQ answers 'Is glutathione safe for all skin tones?', so a batch of six identical fair-skinned women would contradict the copy sitting beside it. The six run ivory, deep brown, light East Asian, golden South Asian, olive Mediterranean and mid-brown mixed heritage. Malcolm picks one; the range exists so the choice is his rather than the engines'.

THE GLOW IS MADE OF LIGHT AND HEALTHY SKIN, NEVER OF COSMETICS OR OF A LIGHTER TONE. Two traps, both negated by name in every slot. First, engines reach for cosmetic highlighter, shimmer powder, glitter, body oil and water droplets the moment they read 'glow' — all barred, so the sheen has to come from a large soft source and hydrated skin. Second, and far more serious on THIS page: nothing may read as skin lightening. The copy claims 'a more even-looking tone' and 'antioxidant defence', not whitening, and the page's FAQ is explicit about all skin tones. No bleaching, no lightening, no before-and-after, no split screen, no tone comparison — a single portrait cannot make the comparison, and the negatives close the door anyway.

SKIN MUST STAY REAL OR THE GLOW IS WORTHLESS. A skincare brand cannot show poreless plastic. Every slot specifies visible fine pores that vary by zone, pale vellus hair catching the light along the jaw and upper lip, a few natural moles or freckles placed asymmetrically, and the faint fine lines that a real thirty-something has at the outer corner of the eye when she smiles. 'No beauty-filter smoothing, no airbrushed skin, no poreless skin, no waxy skin' are all in the global negatives. A candidate that reads as a 3D render or a filtered selfie is out however pretty it is.

AGE IS A SPEC, NOT A SUGGESTION. Thirty to thirty-five, stated in words in every prompt and defended from both sides in the negatives: no teenager, no woman in her twenties, no woman over forty, no grey hair, no deep folds. Engines default young on the word 'beautiful' and old on the word 'skincare'.

THE SMILE IS THE SMALLEST THING AND THE EASIEST TO LOSE. 'Gently' means the corners lifted a little, lips closed or barely parted, the warmth arriving in the eyes as much as the mouth. Grins, laughs, open mouths, full sets of teeth and pouts are all negated, because every engine escalates a smile if it is left unqualified.

CLASS B — no product in frame, no references attached, no product description and no brand identity given to any engine. FLUX.2 is therefore allowed in the run; it invents brand marks but there is nothing here for it to invent, and skin studies are the material it is actually good at. Its one fixed trait still applies — it renders printed digits where none were asked for — so check its candidates at full size.

JUDGE AT 100% AND AGAIN AT RENDER SIZE (roughly 660px on desktop, full width on mobile). Four checks for this wave: HANDS AND EARS, the two things every engine deforms and which no contact sheet shows; EYES, for a matched pair, clean whites and a soft catchlight rather than a ring-light doughnut; SKIN, for texture that survives a 100% zoom without turning to plastic or to noise; and TEETH, on any candidate whose lips have parted further than asked.

slots.title: A · ivory skin, soft window light from one side, three-quarter turn, eyes to camera
slots.prompt:
A beautiful, aspirational beauty photograph for a premium skincare brand: a close-up of one woman's face filling a square frame. This is a real photograph — a high-end campaign portrait taken on a medium-format camera with a short telephoto lens — not an illustration, not a render and not a phone snapshot.

SHE IS BETWEEN THIRTY AND THIRTY-FIVE YEARS OLD and she plainly looks it: a settled adult woman, past her twenties, nowhere near forty. She is a white European woman with warm ivory skin, chestnut-brown hair with a soft natural wave gathered loosely back so a few strands fall free beside her ear, grey-green eyes, and full natural brows that have not been drawn on. A light scatter of small freckles crosses the bridge of her nose and the tops of her cheeks, and there is one small mole below the outer corner of her left eye. Nothing about her is symmetrical.

SHE IS SMILING GENTLY. The corners of her mouth are lifted only a little, her lips are closed or barely parted, and the warmth arrives in her eyes as much as in her mouth — calm, contented, unforced, as if something quietly pleasant has just been said to her. It is not a grin, not a laugh, and no teeth are on show.

HER HEAD IS TURNED ABOUT TWENTY DEGREES AWAY FROM THE CAMERA WHILE HER EYES COME BACK TO THE LENS, so one cheekbone is presented to the light and the far side of her face falls gently away. Her chin is level.

THE LIGHT IS BROAD, SOFT DAYLIGHT ARRIVING FROM ONE SIDE — a tall window just off to her left, close to her, filling most of that side of the frame with even light — and a large soft bounce on the opposite side lifts the shaded half so nothing anywhere on her face goes dark or muddy. The whole picture is bright, clean and high-key. There is a single soft rectangular catchlight in each eye.

THE GLOW IS THE POINT OF THE PICTURE, AND IT IS MADE OF LIGHT ON HEALTHY SKIN, NOT OF COSMETICS. Her skin is freshly hydrated and supple, and the soft light lays a gentle satin sheen along the top of each cheekbone, down the bridge of her nose, across her brow bone, on her cupid's bow and on the point of her chin — a soft luminous bloom that fades away rather than a hard bright edge. A natural warm flush sits across her cheeks and the tip of her nose. Her lips are their own colour, soft and slightly moist. There is no shimmer powder, no highlighter, no glitter, no oil and no water on her skin; the light is doing all of it.

HER SKIN IS REAL AND HOLDS UP AT FULL SIZE, which matters more here than anywhere else. Fine pores are clearly visible and vary by zone — a little more open across the nose and inner cheeks, finer at the temples and along the jaw. Pale vellus hairs catch the sidelight along the jawline and above her lip. There is the faintest fan of fine lines at the outer corner of each eye because she is smiling, and a soft crease where each cheek lifts. Her skin tone is naturally, gently varied rather than one flat colour. It is beautiful skin, not smoothed skin: no filter, no airbrushing, no poreless plastic surface.

SHE WEARS NO MAKEUP. Her brows are natural, her lashes are her own, her lips are unpainted.

THE FRAME, STATED AS EDGES. Her head is large in the square: the top of her hair is cut cleanly by the UPPER EDGE just above her hairline; her chin sits a little way clear of the LOWER EDGE and the tops of her bare shoulders enter the two bottom corners; soft out-of-focus background reaches the LEFT and RIGHT edges beside her cheeks. Her face sits slightly off centre, toward the side she is turned from.

BEHIND HER is a plain pale warm greige wall, softly out of focus, with a gentle gradient from lighter near the window to a touch deeper on the far side. Nothing else is in the room.

No hands and no fingers anywhere in the picture. Clean, luminous, expensive, calm.
